newsitem.title: UK: Courtaulds chief adds to EMU warnings.
newsitem.headline: Courtaulds chief adds to EMU warnings.

text.p: British-based chemicals group Courtaulds Plc on Wednesday added to warnings about the dangers of premature British membership of European Economic and Monetary Union.

In an interview with Reuters, chief executive Gordon Campbell said Barclays Plc chief executive Martin Taylor was "absolutely right" in saying no one knew at what rate sterling should join any single European currency.
In a speech on Tuesday, Taylor said Britain should not consider joining a single currency until its economic cycle was more in line with the rest of Europe.

"If you go in at the wrong rate then it could be a very serious long-term problem for Britain," Campbell said. "At least the ERM had some movement. Once you are in a single currency there is no relief valve...so the entry point is absolutely critical."
Campbell, whose company operates in 43 different countries, said he was "very cautious" about a single currency, which he said was "a sort of stalking horse for the real debate".

"I don't see how you can have a single currency without political union...and the debate is being focused on the currency argument," he added. "I think to some extent this is a phony debate and it is a front because nobody will address the real issue."
Campbell said a single currency with Britain outside would not create serious problems for a company like Courtaulds.
"We don't have problems selling into France, Germany or Italy today, so selling into that bloc ...is going to be no different," he said.
Courtaulds has around 30 percent of its manufacturing in the Britain, with similar portions in continental Europe and the U.S.

"We are going to be an absolute hybrid. We'll have some operations in the single currency and some outside the single currency if sterling doesn't go in, and it strikes me that could be the best of all possible worlds frankly," Campbell said.
